reference.method: Read-only disassembly, matched public symbols, C++ field layouts and explicit base virtual slots. The executable was not run. This artifact contains conclusions and address anchors, not code bytes or disassembly.

facts.topic: food starts the common item-use timer
facts.contract: FoodItemComponentLegacy::use applies its hunger/game-mode checks, including mCanAlwaysEat, obtains the selected item's maximum use duration and calls Player::startUsingItem. The exact golden-apple duration data initializer is not reconstructed here.

The common duration callback decrements ItemInUseComponent.mDuration by one only when the signed value is positive. Zero and negative values are unchanged. The component stores the item at offset0 and duration at offset8.

other duration-system vtable RVA0xEB40870, tick slot0x28 -> RVA0xC611930

facts.topic: normal player completion and item continuity
facts.contract: Player::normalTick compares the held item and selected slot/hand with PlayerItemInUse. A changed count or matching-item state can refresh the copied in-use stack; an incompatible item/slot/hand stops use. At duration zero it optionally calls Player::eat for food and then calls nonvirtual Player::completeUsingItem. No Item::useTimeDepleted invocation is present in that recovered pre-complete branch.
anchors: ItemInUseComponent hash0x05B90AEF and duration-zero check RVA0x1EA813
PDB Player::completeUsingItem has no virtual slot

facts.contract: Player::completeUsingItem publishes ItemCompleteUseEvent before testing ILevel::isClientSide. The client branch goes directly to stopUsingItem, skipping the subsequent item-depletion callback, ItemRelease transaction and CompletedUsingItem packet construction. The server section uses ItemRelease action Use=1 and invokes Item::useTimeDepleted. This is a branch-specific finding; arbitrary event-listener side effects were not completely reconstructed.

facts.topic: food depletion helper is separate from the recovered client branch
facts.contract: Item::useTimeDepleted checks that a player and food component exist and that Actor.mRemoved is false, then invokes IFoodItemComponent::useTimeDepleted. The legacy food helper applies food effects, calls the player's use-item and eat operations and handles item conversion. Neither inspected helper contains a direct GameMode::baseUseItem call. These helpers are invoked by the server section of common completion; their existence alone does not establish a client completion transaction.

facts.topic: continued use intention can start another use
facts.contract: ClientInputCallbacks::handleBuildAction blocks ordinary food re-entry while the local in-use item remains nonempty. After starting a timed use, it calls IClientInstance::resetBai(0x10). The concrete resetBai implementation stores that exact mask in a replacement in-progress intention; it does not clear the intention. ClientInstance::_tickBuildAction can invoke handleBuildAction again on later ticks with the retained mask. When the in-use state is empty and the use-intention path is eligible, it calls GameMode::baseUseItem. Thus continued input can start another use after common completion clears local use state.

exact supplied mask stored RVA0x5DCF4FB; replacement pointer at ClientInstance offset0x290 stored RVA0x5DCF4FD
retained intention load RVA0x5DB3A01 and reuse RVA0x5DB3BAA

facts.topic: native use deadline has a shared block-action role
facts.contract: The recovered air-use path reads the current clock and sets IClientInstance::setNoBlockBreakUntil to that time plus 200,000,000 nanoseconds immediately before baseUseItem. The same deadline is checked in this input path. Its actual interface name is NoBlockBreakUntil; it is not evidence for a dedicated food-completion delay or a global repeat interval for all interactions.

GameMode::baseUseItem constructs an ItemUseInventoryTransaction and, on the client, begins the manager's legacy transaction-request scope, invokes the local use operation, and forwards the complex transaction. Its population callback selects action Use=1, current hand/slot/item, zero block and click positions, face0xFF and the player's current position. This is an ordinary Use/ClickAir transaction, not ItemRelease Use=1.
anchors: selected item helper call RVA0x25B6182 -> RVA0x25B5F50
client Player::sendComplexInventoryTransaction virtual slot0x718 call RVA0x259EE7E

facts.topic: local client transaction forwarding with inventory-manager metadata
facts.contract: The LocalPlayer send-complex-transaction implementation constructs InventoryTransactionPacketPayload and InventoryTransactionPacket, calls _populateLegacyTransactionRequest using the player's inventory manager, then invokes sendNetworkPacket. Having the inventory manager enabled therefore does not by itself prove that ordinary air-use transactions are replaced by Consume stack requests. The complete inventory-request coupling is outside this finding.

ItemStackNetManagerBase pointer read at Player offset0xAB8, RVA0x476A9D8

facts.contract: The matched PDB calls ItemRelease action0 Release and action1 Use. ItemUse action0 is Place, action1 Use, action2 Destroy and action3 UseAsAttack. ActorEvent has no enumerator with value9 in this build. These enum facts do not authorize inventing an outgoing completion packet or establish the behavior of other protocol versions.

comparison.perlin_issue: At the time of investigation, Perlin started food only on a fresh Use press, ended local use at its timer boundary and retained a useConsumed latch until release. The recovered native retained-intention path supports restarting eligible use while input continues. This is a concrete behavioral difference, separate from any unproven dedicated completion-transaction claim.
comparison.custom_server: The supplied log is from a custom PocketMine-derived server. A vanilla-client static branch does not fully specify that server's consumption state machine, and this artifact does not claim a tested end-to-end fix or exact repeated-eating cadence on it.

limitations: Proof is specific to the supplied matched 1.26.51.1/protocol2193 executable. The same behavior in protocol2225 and earlier profiles is not verified by these addresses.

The recovered common client timer branch does not construct a completion ItemRelease Use=1, CompletedUsingItem or ActorEvent9 packet. This is not a global proof that no indirect listener, platform path or other subsystem can send another operation.
ItemCompleteUseEvent dispatch occurs before the client/server branch. Its complete dynamic listener set and side effects were not reconstructed.
The duration callback is proven, but its exact first-tick ordering relative to input was not closed. No exact 32-versus-33 elapsed-tick boundary is asserted here.

Golden apple and enchanted golden apple data initializers, complete consumption inventory actions, full legacy-request decoration, and every custom component use callback remain outside this scoped result.
No native executable was run, no server acceptance test was performed, and no guarantee concerning anti-cheat results is made.
